BEFORE YOU BUY

You don’t have to be a pilot
to choose a great gift.

A few small checks make the difference between a thoughtful surprise and an expensive return.

  1. Start with the person. Their first airplane, a favorite airshow, an off-duty hobby or something they asked for.
  2. Confirm the exact fit. Aircraft plugs, tablet models, case dimensions and clothing sizes all matter.
  3. Check the delivered total. Include tax and shipping, and read the arrival estimate and return terms.
  4. Choose technical equipment together. The pilot’s own requirements matter more than a general ranking.

Ask without giving away the surprise

  • What airplane did you first learn in?
  • What is one thing in your flight bag you wish you could replace?
  • Do you have a link to the exact version?
  • Would you rather choose equipment together or get something for home?

Leave room for their preferences

A model of a meaningful aircraft, a book on a favorite subject or a modest everyday accessory can be easier to get right than equipment. For headsets, simulator hardware and tablet accessories, an exact wishlist link is more useful than a surprise.
